source_text_bechina_scan.result: NO explicit bechina formula statements found in this Torah.
source_text_bechina_scan.explanation: Torah LM2 #117 is a logical/explanatory teaching (a short responsum-style text). Its entire argument is structured as cause-and-effect chains (eitza), not as conceptual identifications (bechina). The Rebbe proves a point using rational argument ('מימה נפשך: if A then B, if not A then C') and Talmudic proofs, not by equating the essential natures of concepts.

evil_mirror_analysis.note: This Torah is structured around a single polarity: the domain of high holiness (קדושה גבוהה) on the positive side and the domain of the yetzer hara / judgments / impurity on the negative side. However, neither side is built from explicit bechina clusters. The evil domain concepts (יצר הרע, קיטרוגים, דינים, טומאה) are connected to each other and to the positive concepts only via eitza (causal) relationships, not via bechina (shared-nature) relationships. Therefore no evil package can be formally constructed.
evil_mirror_analysis.implicit_evil_structure: יצר הרע ← מהשתלשלות הדינים ← קיטרוגים ← entering high holiness — this is a pure eitza chain.
evil_mirror_analysis.implicit_good_structure: קדושה גבוהה → expels טומאה טמונה → enables תיקון — this is also a pure eitza chain.

analysis_notes.torah_structure_note: LM2 Torah 117 is a short halakhic-ethical responsum (8 lines). Its argumentative style is entirely logical/eitza: premise → counterargument → resolution → proof from Talmud → proof from Torah narrative. It contains zero explicit bechina formula statements. This is consistent with its genre — a practical clarification rather than a mystical teaching that maps conceptual domains.
